@thatangeldude I wouldn’t say Equivalent Exchange was completely debunked by love. The ending is more about showing that it isn’t a universal law . Equivalent Exchange still applies to alchemy, Ed literally gives up his Gate to get Al back. What gets challenged is the idea that everything in life has to be an equal transaction. Winry offering more than Ed asked for and Al’s “10 becomes 11” idea both show that people can give more than they receive. So I think the ending is expanding the philosophy rather than simply debunking it. And let me explain deeply The series doesn't suddenly establish:
“Equivalent Exchange was completely false.” In fact, Ed's final narration still says that sacrifices are necessary and that you can't gain something without losing something first. And Ed literally gives up his Gate of Truth to restore Alphonse's body. That's still a genuine sacrifice or exchange within the story. Here FMAB doesn't completely reject Equivalent Exchange. It rejects the idea that Equivalent Exchange is a sufficient philosophy for understanding human life.
